Callers fn-xw-publish-initial-file (1758-1759, staging/.init-PID-HEX) and fn-xw-secret-rotate (1845-1848, keys/.node-secret-PID-HEX.stage) return w without unlinking the stage. The native rotate (host/native/io.lisp:3940-3946) also unlinks only on a rename failure.
fix: Unlink the stage path when the write or fsync fails, both here and in io.lisp's fnn-node-secret-rotate and fnn-publish-initial-file. Or make the keys/ stage names part of a namespace the recovery sweep collects.

reviewer: store-write-host.lisp:1742-1750 fn-xw-write-new returns the write or fsync error without unlinking the O_EXCL stage. fn-xw-secret-rotate (around 1845-1848) unlinks the stage only when the rename fails. So a failed write or fsync leaves keys/.node-secret-<pid>-<hex>.stage holding part of the fresh root, under a new random name on every retry. Nothing in host, books or tools sweeps keys/ for .stage names; the staging sweeps cover staging/. The native rotate (io.lisp:3938-3946) closes in unwind-protect but likewise never unlinks after a write or fsync failure. The file is a leftover of secret material plus disk litter, but it is never used as authority.
scenario: `store ROOT node-secret rotate` fails with ENOSPC or EIO partway through writing the new root, or at its fsync. keys/.node-secret-<pid>-<hex>.stage is left holding a prefix of the fresh secret root. The staging sweep covers staging/, not keys/, so nothing ever removes it. Each failed retry leaves another file under a fresh random name.
title: Node-secret staging files with partial key material are left behind when a write or fsync fails
